source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 6: Show that the determinant equals (x+4)(x-2)^2 (book page 60).

blocks.explanation:
Dikhana hai ke yeh determinant \((x+4)(x-2)^2\) ke barabar hai.
Har row ka total \(x + 2 + 2 = x + 4\) hai: jawab ka pehla factor yahin se aayega.
Plan: \(C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\), \(x+4\) bahar, zeros banayein, triangular shakal se jawab.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} x & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & x & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & x \end{vmatrix}\)
Saabit karna hai: \(\Delta = (x+4)(x-2)^2\)
Tareeqa: Property vii (columns jama; rows minus), Property v (factor bahar), Property viii (triangular determinant). Expand kar ke cubic ko factorise karna mushkil hota, is liye properties behtar hain.

Teeno columns ko column 1 mein jama karein
\[C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} x+4 & 2 & 2 \\ x+4 & x & 2 \\ x+4 & 2 & x \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har row mein ek \(x\) aur do 2 hain, total \(x + 4\). Property vii se value wohi.

Column 1 se \(x+4\) bahar nikalein
\[\Delta = (x+4)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & x & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & x \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: Property v: column 1 ki har entry mein \(x + 4\) common hai, woh ek dafa bahar aa gaya.

Row 1 ko row 2 aur 3 mein se minus karein
\[R_2 - R_1 \to R_2,\quad R_3 - R_1 \to R_3\]
\[\Delta = (x+4)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & x-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & x-2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(1 - 1 = 0\), \(x - 2\), \(2 - 2 = 0\). Diagonal ke neeche sab zero: upper triangular.

Diagonal multiply karein
\[\Delta = (x+4) \cdot 1 \cdot (x-2)(x-2)\]
\[= (x+4)(x-2)^2\]
Kyun: Property viii: triangular determinant = diagonal ka product. \((x-2)\) do dafa aaya, is liye square.

Tasdeeq (number rakh kar)
\[x = 0:\ \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 0 - 2(-4) + 2(4) = 16\]
\[(0+4)(0-2)^2 = 16 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(x = 0\) rakh kar row 1 ke along expand kiya: \(-2(0 - 4) + 2(4 - 0) = 16\). Formula se bhi 16. Dono barabar.
